how: Mission Cliffs (Touchstone Climbing) has a 2,000 sq ft bouldering area with day passes and intro-to-climbing classes.

Saint Mary's Chinese Language School in Chinatown runs recurring beginner and intermediate Chinese calligraphy classes; the Japanese American Association of Northern California holds Japanese calligraphy workshops.
Maker Studio in Hayes Valley lists a Sewing Social Club session with an intro to embroidery, and other embroidery workshops are offered around the Bay.
GGNRA offers ranger-led walks, and Meetup groups run weekly nature walks at Fort Funston and the Presidio.
GGNRA lists tide pooling among its visitor activities, with sites such as Mori Point.

how: Beginner hip hop dance classes run in Mission Bay and Potrero Hill studios, but no breaking-specific class was confirmed.
Community volunteer gardening runs at Alemany Farm through Nature in the City, and an East Bay permaculture guild meets at PLACE, but personal allotment plots were not confirmed.
Rug tufting workshops run daily at studios at 575 Sutter St (Union Square) and 360 Ritch St (SoMa).
Gamescape SF is a Divisadero Street board game store and event space with weekly game nights; Victory Point Cafe in Berkeley offers open board game play for a small fee.
The Mechanics' Institute Chess Club at 57 Post St hosts USCF/FIDE-rated tournaments, monthly socials and classes from beginner to advanced; Pawn Shop Chess Club SF also meets free at Alamo Square.
Gamescape SF stocks D&D and Pathfinder and hosts RPG nights, while Meetup groups (SF LGBT D&D Group, Bay Area Table Top RPG Network) run Adventurers League and Pathfinder campaigns.

how: Hands On Gourmet in Dogpatch runs hands-on cooking classes such as handmade ravioli, and other SF hosts list pasta and dumpling classes.
Breakthrough Sushi holds sushi-making dinner classes several evenings a week at Hotel Kabuki in Japantown.
Noisebridge hackerspace runs Woodhacking Mondays (all skill levels) and fabrication safety classes; equipment is free to use with donations welcome.
Noisebridge teaches a 3D printing class every other Sunday and members can use the printers; equipment is free with donations welcome.
A San Mateo Radio Club monthly meeting (Southern Peninsula Emergency Communications System) is listed on Meetup.
Noisebridge hosts weekly software-infrastructure and hacking nights and Meetup lists groups such as SF Rust Study Group and Hackers/Founders.
Noisebridge hosts Circuit Hacking Monday and an Arduino for Total Newbies class, with soldering and electronics benches open to the public.
SF Bay Area Game Jamming & Game Design and Noisebridge (weekly Gamebridge and a monthly Godot meetup) run game development meetups.
Noisebridge runs laser cutter safety certification sessions on Sundays (limited availability).
Emporium Arcade Bar in Alamo Square is an arcade bar with classic machines and events.
Lore Speakeasy and Escape Room in the Inner Mission operates an escape room alongside game events.
Bay Area Mahjong Meetup holds Mahjong Monday drop-ins at Mamahuhu in Noe Valley and Marin Mahjong runs free social play at libraries and rec centres.
Gamescape SF has a Miniature Games department stocking Warhammer 40K, Age of Sigmar and Kill Team and runs a weekly game-night schedule.
Mission Bowling Club in the Inner Mission and Lucky Strike in Mission Bay run bowling leagues and community nights.
Chocolate classes and tasting events (e.g. a Recchiuti chocolate experience, Manny's chocolate club) are listed, but no bean-to-bar course was confirmed.
Elixir in Mission Dolores and The Alembic in the Haight run cocktail classes, including "Great Cocktails: An Introduction to Mixology".
Hands On Gourmet in Dogpatch lists a Dim Sum Cooking Class covering soup dumplings and more.
Telescope Coffee in SoMa runs espresso and milk steaming classes, which cover the barista skills behind latte art.
Mechanics' Institute in Union Square runs a multi-session Wine Appreciation Series, and wine dinners and tastings are listed across the city.
SFMOMA, 151 Third St, houses modern and contemporary art galleries; adult admission is $30 and under-19s are free.
SpanFran runs Spanish/French language exchanges at Muddy Waters Cafe and several Meetup groups run Japanese, Mandarin, German and French exchanges.
SFMOMA, 151 Third St, is one of many major museums; adult admission is $30 and under-19s are free.

The California Academy of Sciences in Golden Gate Park combines an aquarium, planetarium, rainforest and natural history museum; Chabot Space & Science Center in Oakland adds free Friday and Saturday telescope nights.
Toastmasters clubs such as Townsend Toastmasters, Oakland Warehouse Toastmasters and Peninsula Toastmasters hold regular meetings listed on Meetup.
Hackathons are listed on Meetup, e.g. an ODSC AI x Nebius hackathon, alongside weekly civic-tech hack nights.
Noisebridge runs Arduino for Total Newbies and a robotics meetup that requires no prior experience.
Ace Makerspace in Oakland offers costume-making workshops and an SF anime club meetup lists cosplay guests, but no dedicated cosplay club was confirmed.
Noisebridge hosts fortnightly fighting-game nights (School of Melee) and Meetup lists local gaming groups, but no dedicated esports venue was confirmed.
San Francisco Go Club holds Play Go and Socialize sessions on Fridays and Sundays, and Tri-Valley Go Players meet weekly in Pleasanton.
San Francisco Pub Quiz runs trivia on Mondays at The Sycamore and Wednesdays at The Willows; Oakland Trivia Night meets at Ghost Town.

activity: Artisan bread and pastry baking courses
how: Hands On Gourmet in Dogpatch and other hosts run baking classes covering sourdough starters, challah and pastry.
Mercurius Beer Lab in the Inner Mission teaches beer brewing classes (Brew It Yourself: Beer Making at Home, and a full-grain 102 course).
Shumei San Francisco Center runs Japanese tea meditation sessions and ChaTo in Japantown hosts Japanese tea tastings, but a formal chado school was not confirmed.
Sourdough Starter and Sip & Sourdough baking workshops are listed in SoMa and at the Blue Heron Boathouse in Golden Gate Park.
The Whisky Shop in Union Square holds frequent single-malt and bourbon tasting events.
EcoCenter at Heron's Head Park in the Central Waterfront lists guided bird walks (e.g. Birds, Bay and Belonging), and GGNRA lists birding among visitor activities.
Gamescape SF has a trading card games department (Magic: The Gathering, Pokemon, Lorcana, One Piece) and hosts prerelease events; a Magic Casual Players Meetup meets Sundays.
The Koshland San Francisco History Center on the 6th floor of the Main Library holds the city archives, manuscripts, photographs, maps and newspapers for public research.

how: San Francisco Public Library hosts a workshop on writing memoir, short story and essay at the Main Library, and Union Arts Center runs book-writing classes.
The Japanese American Association of Northern California in Japantown hosts regular cultural workshops, e.g. Japanese calligraphy.

how: San Francisco Historical Society operates a walking-tours programme (sfhistory.org/tours) and Meetup runs neighbourhood history tours such as Duboce Park Victorians.
SF German Stammtisch holds monthly German-speaking meetups at Paprika and Salesforce Park, but no formal German course was confirmed.
SF Japanese Language Exchange meets Wednesdays and a Berkeley Japanese-English exchange meets Tuesdays, but no formal course was confirmed.
Spanish-English language exchanges run in SF and Berkeley (SpanFran at Muddy Waters Cafe, Berkeley Language Exchange), but no formal Spanish course was confirmed.
SF Philosophy Club and San Francisco Philosophy Reading Group hold paper and reading discussions, and a Socrates Cafe runs online.
Poetry in SF Chinatown holds a monthly 3rd Saturday poetry event and Meetup lists poetry-inclusive open mics.
San Francisco Historical Society runs a History Live! lecture series and events schedule.
Golden Gate National Recreation Area manages WWII-era sites including Fort Point and Battery East.
Refuse Refuse - San Francisco Cleanups runs weekly KEEP Ocean Beach cleans and monthly Crissy Field and Fort Miley cleanup days; Save the Bay also runs volunteer shoreline restoration.
East Bay Dipping Society holds group ocean dips and Alameda Open Water Swimming meets weekly, but no dedicated ice-bath venue was confirmed.
